subject: Urgent: node-slot audit for late-stage Apexence deal
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: node-slot audit for late-stage Apexence deal

Team —

Apexence is moving to final contract this week (HS deal APX-2109). They asked us to guarantee dedicated capacity for a 24/7 inference pod for their production launch (Q3 ramp). Before legal signs off on the SLA we need an internal confirmation of exact node slots we can pledge and any soft-fallthroughs.

Quick context: their workload is a mix of 8k-token chat + batch embed generation. They requested:
- 6x high-memory T4-equivalent workers (sustained)
- 2x optional GPU-heavy burst nodes for peak inference spikes

What I need from ops/tiling folks:
1) A one-page inventory snapshot showing available contiguous node slots through September (include region us-west-2 preferred).
2) Any scheduling/tiling constraints that would prevent us from block-reserving contiguous capacity for 90 days.
3) If we can only offer partial capacity, outline compatible fallback (quantized flavors, reduced concurrency, or scheduled nightly batch windows).

I attached a brief requirements summary and their proposed node map (proposed_node_map_v2.pdf). Please mark any hard blockers; the customer expects an internal commit by EOD Friday so Legal can pin the SLA.

Thanks —
Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: proposed_node_map_v2.pdf (summary), inventory_snapshot_20290612.csv (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: node-slot audit for late-stage Apexence deal

Dev —

Thanks for the heads-up. I pulled the evening inventory snapshot (attached) and did a quick tile check for us-west-2. Highlights:
- Contiguous high-mem pool: 5 full slots available immediately, 2 more probable by 2029-07-03 after scheduled maintenance window (node reclamation).
- Burst-capable GPUs: 1 dedicated A500-class slot free now; second can be carved via preemptible pool with a 2–4 hour warm-up depending on image pulls.
- Thermal/placement constraints: the high-mem nodes needed for 8k sequences require contiguous nvlink adjacency for optimal perf — we only have one contiguous block of 5 today.

Options to satisfy their ask today:
A) Offer 5 contiguous + 1 burst now; commit to 6th contiguous by 2029-07-03 (soft hold).
B) Offer 6 non-contiguous immediately with a routing policy that pins traffic to compatible variants (minor perf delta).
C) If they insist on guaranteed contiguous 6x right away, we'd need to re-home an internal experiment pod (2-week lead) or escalate to inventory swap.

I've added the raw CSV to the attachments (inventory_snapshot_20290612.csv) and flagged OPS-7843 for a follow-up runbook on how fast we can bump to contiguous 6.

If Legal needs a firm date we can commit to option A with the 07/03 contingency. Confirm whether Apexence will accept a 07/03 activation for the 6th slot.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Capacity Planning Lead | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: inventory_snapshot_20290612.csv (live query export)

From: Claire Jennings <claire@apexence.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Jun 2029 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: node-slot audit for late-stage Apexence deal

Dev / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick work here. Apexence is comfortable with a staged activation as long as:
- We get 5 guaranteed contiguous nodes at contract signing
- The 6th contiguous node is activated no later than 2029-07-05 (we can accept 07/05 but prefer 07/03)
- The burst node availability is contractually bounded as "best-effort preemptible" with a 2-hour warm-up clause

If you can send back a short note we can attach to the Master Services Agreement that outlines the above (we don't need internal ops detail, just the commitment language and dates).

Also: can you confirm whether reduced-precision (int8) model variants are in scope if we need temporary capacity headroom during peak launches?

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Jennings
Head of Infrastructure | Apexence, Inc.
claire@apexence.com

All —

I ran a quick feasibility for the firm commitment language Legal wants. Summary for the note we can hand to Claire:

- Guarantee: 5 contiguous high-memory nodes (us-west-2) effective at contract signature date.
- Staged activation: 6th contiguous node scheduled for activation no later than 2029-07-03 (we will target 07/01, 07/03 is the latest acceptable).
- Burst: one A500-class burst node labeled "best-effort preemptible" with an estimated warm-up of 2 hours; second burst node is available from our preemptible pool but not guaranteed in the baseline SLA.
- Precision fallback: int8 variants are supported for up to 30% of peak traffic as an agreed temporary throttle; this will require a quick config change on the deployment and model quantization profile (we will own the rollout).
- Escalation: if contiguous 6 cannot be met by 07/03 we will provide a documented remediation plan within 48 hours and a credit schedule in line with our standard SLA exceptions.

Ben, please confirm the 07/03 activation gating (re-home vs scheduled maintenance) is accurate. Once Ben thumbs-up I'll send this as a short commitment note to Claire for attachment to the MSA.

—Karthik

Head of Infrastructure Partnerships | Redwood Inference
